summary: Preinstall fetches Bun runtime and executes 727KB obfuscated payload under a UI-button package
details: The npm package @onereach/si-a-button@0.0.3 is advertised as a Vue UI button component but ships a preinstall lifecycle hook (`node setup.mjs`) that, on `npm install`, downloads the Bun language runtime from GitHub releases (https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v.../...) and then invokes that runtime via execFileSync to run `math_init.js`, a 727KB heavily obfuscated sibling file (string-array/dictionary obfuscation, hex-encoded identifiers, shuffled numeric tables consistent with an obfuscator.io-style payload). The preinstall script `setup.mjs` is itself obfuscated (`_0xNNNN` identifier renaming, per-function proxy dictionaries). A UI button component has no legitimate reason to install an alternate language runtime and execute opaque code under it at install time. The alternate-runtime-dropper pattern (using Bun to run the payload rather than Node) evades Node-focused static analysis, and the obfuscated payload's actual behavior cannot be inspected without dedicated deobfuscation. Installing this package causes arbitrary attacker-authored code to execute on the installer's machine.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
